survey: Two flip-flops lie side by side and point the same way. The toe ends are at the lower left and the heels at the upper right. The camera looks down from above and slightly to the front-right. Both soles show their top face plus a strip of thickness along the right and front edges. These side strips are about equally deep on both soles, and their short vertical edges lean the same small amount, so the two soles share one camera. Both soles lie flat on the same unseen ground plane, and their long edges are near-parallel (blue ~58° on both). The right sandal sits slightly lower and nearer, and it is about the same size as the left one, which is acceptable for a mild stylized view. On each sandal, the yellow Y-strap rises from a short toe post, which stands upright along the same "up" direction as the sole's side edges. The two strap arms arch back and tuck into slots on the sole. The arms are raised above the sole, so they appear shifted up and to the left, which matches a camera to the right and above. The left arm's arch reaching past the sole outline is explained by that height. The tread dots near each toe appear as small flattened ovals. They sit in rows that follow the sole's outline and shrink slightly toward the far end, so they lie on the surface correctly. Both straps are drawn at the same angle and cast shadows that agree. Nothing breaks the single viewpoint.
